title: How To Handle Unfair Criticism And Turn It Into Your Advantage
author: Michael Linsin
summary: In a more personal, reflective piece, Michael Linsin addresses the sting of unfair criticism — a principal misjudging a moment out of context, a colleague spreading an untrue rumor — that especially affects newer teachers or those new to a school. He argues these moments, while demoralizing, ultimately don't matter, because sustained good work will eventually be recognized: 'it will also be corrected.' Linsin shares a personal memory of a principal who left handwritten notes of encouragement, contrasting it with today's more impersonal school cultures, and urges teachers to remember what unfair judgment and loneliness felt like in order to become mentors for newer or underestimated colleagues. The article reframes unfair criticism as fuel for determination and mental toughness rather than something to resolve through self-justification, and closes with a call to become 'the person you needed' for others.
points: Unfair criticism — misjudged moments, out-of-context observations, untrue rumors — happens to nearly every teacher, especially those newer to a school.
Trying to explain yourself or correct the record in the moment often backfires; staying the course and continuing good work is the more effective long-term response.
Sustained quality work eventually earns recognition, even if it takes months or years, particularly at larger or more challenging schools.
Unfair criticism can be reframed as fuel that sharpens determination, mental toughness, and ultimately produces greater excellence.
Teachers are encouraged to remember the loneliness of being misunderstood and use it to become mentors and encouragers for newer, quieter, or underestimated colleagues.
quotes: At some point, unfair criticism happens to everybody. Especially if you’re a newer teacher or new to a school and have yet to establish your reputation.
Those moments when the boss walks in at just the wrong time, or the long months when no one knows who you are, what you stand for, or the excellent work you're doing, don't matter.
Because unfair criticism keeps you on your toes. It forges your determination and mental toughness. It produces even greater excellence.

You see, if instead of worrying over something you have no control over, or worse, trying to explain yourself—which often backfires—you put your head down and stay the course, then your true reputation will reveal itself to everyone on campus.
When I was a new teacher, my principal would leave notes of praise and encouragement in my mailbox.
Let it inspire you to be the mentor, the encourager, and the leader that newer, quieter, or underestimated colleagues aren’t getting from anyone else.
